ghs.assessment: Standard Hepburn renders 堂島 as Dōjima. 'Doujima' uses a nonstandard vowel spelling.

rows.jp: 「その極道みたいな苗字とは裏腹にキュートな声は……遊紗ちゃん？　あいてるからどーぞ」
rows.en: “That cute voice could only belong to Yusa, despite the yakuza surname. It’s open—come on in.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "A gangster-like surname associated with a conversely kyute voice... Yusa-chan? It's open, do come in!"
ghs.assessment: The line misspells 'cute' as 'kyute,' and the retained Japanese given name 遊紗 requires standard Hepburn Yūsa rather than 'Yusa.' The opening noun phrase is also ungrammatically attached.
ghs.remedy: Use standard Hepburn for the proper name and grammatical English for the contrast.

highlights.text: Taichi: "A gangster-like surname associated with a conversely kyute voice... Yusa-chan? It's open, do come in!"

rows.jp: ドアがおそるおそる開き、美少女が立っていた。
rows.en: The door opened timidly, revealing a beautiful girl.

ghs.en: Slowly and carefully the door opens, and there stood a beautiful girl.
ghs.assessment: The source presents two past actions in sequence. The English shifts from present 'opens' to past 'stood' within one sentence.

highlights.text: Slowly and carefully the door opens, and there stood a beautiful girl.

rows.en: I sat her down and poured her a glass of barley tea.

ghs.en: I let her sit, and lay out some barley tea.

rows.en: We talked about this and that.

rows.jp: 「あの、わたし今日が誕生日なんです」

ghs.en: Yusa: "Uhm, it's that today would be my birthday."
ghs.assessment: The source directly states that today is her birthday. 'Today would be my birthday' introduces an unsupported conditional mood.

highlights.text: Yusa: "Uhm, it's that today would be my birthday."

ghs.assessment: 'It was, right' is not an idiomatic response to learning the fact.

rows.jp: 「それでですね、これ……お誕生日プレゼントです」
rows.en: “So, um... this is a birthday present.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "So then, here... a birthday present!"

rows.jp: 「ええと……とりあえず、ありがとう。でも、あれ？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Uhmmm... first of all, thank you. But, uh...?"

rows.jp: 「それと、交換日記を明日提出できたらなと思ったので……」
rows.en: “And I thought perhaps I could turn in our exchange diary tomorrow...”

ghs.en: Yusa: "And also, I thought, so I could hand in the exchange diary tomorrow..."
ghs.assessment: The source says she hoped she could submit the exchange diary tomorrow. The English leaves 'I thought, so I could' as an incomplete causal construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'And I was hoping I could turn in the exchange diary tomorrow...'

highlights.text: Yusa: "And also, I thought, so I could hand in the exchange diary tomorrow..."

rows.jp: 「じゃあとりあえず交換日記と、それとこれは俺からの誕生日プレゼント」
rows.en: “Here’s the exchange diary. And this is a birthday present from me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "So, first of all your exchange diary, and also, this is a birthday present from me."

rows.jp: この娘は驚くと絶句する癖があった。
rows.en: Whenever this girl was startled, she tended to lose her voice.

ghs.en: This young lady has the bad habit of losing words when surprised, don't she.
ghs.assessment: The source neutrally says she has a habit of becoming speechless when surprised. 'Bad habit' adds disapproval, and 'don't she' is ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She has a habit of falling speechless whenever she is surprised.'

highlights.text: This young lady has the bad habit of losing words when surprised, don't she.

rows.jp: 「さてと、じゃ家まで送ろうか」
rows.en: “All right. Shall I walk you home?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well then, let's see you home."

rows.jp: さっきの倍くらいに絶句した。
rows.en: This time, she was twice as speechless as before.

ghs.en: Her loss of words about doubled from before.

rows.jp: 「もう夜だし、ちょっと危ない人もいるからね」
rows.en: “It’s already dark, and there are some dangerous people out there.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, it's night now, isn't it."
ghs.assessment: Taichi explains that it is already night and that some dangerous people are around. The English omits the danger that motivates his offer to escort her.
ghs.remedy: It's already night, and there are some dangerous people around.

highlights.text: Well, it's night now, isn't it.

rows.en: And so I walked her home.

ghs.en: And so, I took her home.

rows.jp: 「その質問、毎回しますよね、太一さん？」
rows.en: “You ask me that every time, don’t you, Taichi?”

ghs.en: Yusa: "That question... you just ask me that every time, right Taichi-san?"
ghs.assessment: The vocative needs punctuation, and 'you just ask me that every time' has unnatural adverb placement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You ask that every time, don't you, Taichi?'

highlights.text: Yusa: "That question... you just ask me that every time, right Taichi-san?"

rows.jp: 「難しくてよくわかりませんですけど……はい」
rows.en: “It is difficult, so I don’t understand very well... but yes.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "That is a bit complicated so I do not really understand but... yes!"

ghs.assessment: きょーしゅー represents the sound of 教習, training or instruction. 'Trainingful' is not an English word.
ghs.remedy: Use a legible first member of the sound chain, such as 'Training.'

ghs.assessment: The repeated きょーしゅー continues the same broad sound. 'Calisthenics' narrows it to physical exercise and weakens the pivot to the following homophones.
ghs.remedy: Keep the same sound-linked rendering used in the preceding line.

ghs.assessment: 郷愁 is nostalgia. 'To reduce homesickness?' invents an action and purpose rather than naming the homophone.
強襲 means an assault or raid. 'Violence' is broader and loses the exact homophone in the sequence.
強襲 means assault or raid and resolves the preceding homophone chain. 'Training in violence' combines two earlier mistranslations and does not name the word.

ghs.en:
Intense, turbulent, or furious
and often destructive action.
ghs.assessment: The source immediately glosses the word as attacking fiercely. The English substitutes a generic dictionary-style definition of intense or destructive action and omits the attack.

highlights.text:
Intense, turbulent, or furious
and often destructive action.

rows.jp: 俺はこの言葉が、好きだな。

ghs.en: I really love those words, don't I!
ghs.assessment: この言葉 is singular, 'this word.' 'Those words' changes the number, while 'don't I' adds self-confirmation.

highlights.text: I really love those words, don't I!

ghs.en: I laugh so hard within my dream.
ghs.assessment: 嗤う is a derisive laugh or sneer. 'Laugh so hard' describes intensity rather than scorn and adds a degree absent from the source.

highlights.text: I laugh so hard within my dream.

rows.jp: 沈んだ感情はすぐに深淵に呑まれる。
rows.en: The sunken emotion is soon swallowed by the abyss.

ghs.en: Sinking sentiments that are quickly swallowed by the abyss.

rows.jp: シニシズムの虚無を思わせるメッキは溶解し、むきだしになっ%Nたカケラが……巨大な母体にまざって、戯(ざ)れる。
rows.en: The veneer that evoked cynicism’s void dissolves, and the naked%Nfragment mingles with the vast matrix... and plays.

ghs.en: If killing needs be, killing it will be.
ghs.assessment: 殺さば殺す is retaliatory: if the enemy kills, kill in return. 'If killing needs be' changes that conditional relation into a general judgment of necessity.

highlights.text: If killing needs be, killing it will be.
